identity.title: Food Safety Plan for Ready-to-Eat Hummus and Bean Dips

page_refs.issuer: not issued by agency; company-prepared document

scan.summary: This is a Food Safety Plan prepared by Willamette Valley Foods under the FDA's Food Safety Modernization Act (FSMA) Preventive Controls rule. It describes the company's system for identifying hazards in their refrigerated ready-to-eat hummus and bean dip production, defining critical control points, and documenting monitoring, corrective actions, and verification activities. The plan became effective May 12, 2025, and is available to FDA and Oregon Department of Agriculture inspectors.
scan.freshness_note: This plan is dated May 12, 2025, and is 16 months old as of today (September 25, 2026). FSMA requires plans to be reviewed and updated at least annually if there are significant changes to the facility, process, or products. No document states this plan has been reviewed or updated since May 2025. Ask whether a revised plan exists or whether the plan has been reviewed and re-approved.

gaps.title: Missing annual re-evaluation date or review cycle
gaps.description: FSMA requires food safety plans to be reanalyzed if there are any significant changes to the facility, process, or products, but the rule also expects regular review. The document states the plan is 'effective' May 12, 2025, but does not document that it has been reviewed annually or state when the next formal review is due. A gap appears when the current date exceeds one year from the effective date without documented review.
gaps.fix: Add a dated line stating 'This plan was reviewed and reaffirmed on [date]' or 'Next scheduled review: [date]'. Include in section 7 (Verification) a statement such as 'The PCQI reviews the entire food safety plan annually and documents any changes or confirmation that the plan remains current.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.155(b) requires the plan to be reanalyzed if there are any significant changes; good practice requires documented annual review
gaps.locator: page 1 (effective date only); should also appear in section 7 (Verification)

gaps.title: No statement on supplier verification frequency or re-audit requirements
gaps.description: Section 8 states that tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers with a current third-party audit certificate, but does not specify how often the audit certificate must be renewed or what 'current' means. For a refrigerated product with a 45-day shelf life, a supplier's audit certificate could be 12 months old and still be called 'current,' but FSMA expectations vary by product risk and company practice.
gaps.fix: Clarify in section 8: 'Approved suppliers must provide a third-party audit certificate dated within [12 months / other period]. The approved supplier list is reviewed [quarterly / annually], and suppliers with certificates expiring within 60 days are contacted for renewal.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.150 (Supplier verification program); FSMA guidance on supplier audits
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: No defined action for out-of-specification lot certificates of analysis
gaps.description: Section 8 requires a certificate of analysis for each lot of tahini and dry beans, but does not specify what happens if the results fall outside acceptable ranges. For example, if a lot shows unexpected levels of moisture, pathogen testing, or metal content, there is no corrective action documented.
gaps.fix: Add to section 8: 'If a certificate of analysis shows results outside [specified ranges], the lot is not accepted or is quarantined pending investigation. The quality manager documents the reason for rejection.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.150(b) requires the company to verify that suppliers are producing food safely; implied by best practice
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.title: No documented recall or traceability procedure
gaps.description: The plan documents monitoring, corrective actions, and record-keeping, but does not include a recall procedure. FSMA requires facilities to establish and follow procedures to quickly identify affected product and remove it from commerce if a food safety hazard is found. The plan should describe how lots are traceable and what the company would do in a recall scenario.
gaps.fix: Add a new section (e.g., section 11): 'Recall procedure. All tubs are coded with a date code and batch number. In the event of a recall, [Product Identification]: Lot [Number] produced on [Date] with shelf life until [Date] will be traced to [distribution channels]. The PCQI will notify [management, customers, FDA]. A mock recall drill is conducted [annually / other frequency].'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.80 (Recall plan); 21 CFR 117.139 (Traceability); FSMA guidance on recalls

gaps.title: No statement on product allergen cross-contact risk beyond sesame
gaps.description: The hazard analysis (section 3) identifies sesame as an allergen requiring a preventive control, and the preventive controls section (section 4) describes scheduling hummus last in the day with a full washdown. However, the plan does not address whether other allergens (tree nuts, legumes, etc.) are present in other products made on the same line, whether raw materials are screened for undeclared allergens, or what the risk is from sesame cross-contact with bean-only dips.
gaps.fix: Add to the facility description (section 1) or allergen section: 'The facility produces [list products]. Products containing the allergens [list] are made on the same line as hummus and bean dips. Cross-contact risk is managed by [product scheduling, line cleaning, separate equipment, etc.].' Alternatively, clarify in section 3 whether the sesame allergen hazard applies only to hummus or to all products.
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.460 (Allergen controls); FDA Allergen Labeling Guidance
gaps.locator: Section 1 (facility description, page 2) or section 3 (hazard analysis, page 3)
gaps.quote: Products are labeled with the allergen statement "Contains: sesame" for all hummus items.

gaps.title: No sampling plan for raw materials beyond supplier verification
gaps.description: Section 8 requires suppliers to provide a certificate of analysis for each lot, but the plan does not state whether the company verifies this certificate (e.g., by spot-checking lots) or relies solely on supplier submission. For a food safety hazard like Salmonella in beans, a certificate from the supplier may not be sufficient without independent verification.
gaps.fix: Add to section 8 or 7: 'The company [will / does not] conduct independent testing on [percentage] of incoming lots of tahini and beans. Samples are tested for [hazards] by [method, laboratory]. Results are reviewed and trended [frequency].'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.150(b) (Supplier verification); best practice in FSMA guidance
gaps.quote: Tahini and dry beans are received only from approved suppliers who provide a current third-party audit certificate and a certificate of analysis for each lot.

gaps.description: Section 6 states: 'If a Listeria spp. swab is positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since the last negative swab is held pending investigation.' However, there is no documented procedure for how long product is held, what 'investigation' entails, who approves release or destruction, or whether finished product is tested for Listeria when environmental swabs are positive.
gaps.fix: Expand section 6: 'If a Listeria spp. swab is positive: (1) The site is cleaned and re-swabbed within [timeframe]. (2) Adjacent sites are swabbed. (3) Product made on that line since the last negative swab is held and tested for Listeria monocytogenes [by method]. (4) If product tests negative, it is [released / destroyed / other action] and documented. (5) The PCQI investigates the root cause [within timeframe] and documents findings.'
gaps.citation: 21 CFR 117.160 (Corrective actions); FDA Listeria Guidance for RTE Foods
gaps.quote: If a Listeria spp. swab is positive, the site is cleaned and re-swabbed, adjacent sites are added, and product made on that line since the last negative swab is held pending investigation.

expected_missing.why: A small company would typically have a procedure document describing how suppliers are added, evaluated, and monitored; the plan references an 'approved supplier list' but does not describe the approval process.
expected_missing.basis: Similar food manufacturing companies typically maintain a separate supplier approval SOP

expected_missing.title: Change control or process deviation log
expected_missing.why: When the facility, products, or processes change (e.g., new equipment, new ingredient supplier, recipe change), companies document the change and whether the food safety plan requires updating. This is not mentioned in the plan.
expected_missing.basis: FSMA best practice and similar company programs

expected_missing.title: Mock recall or traceability drill results
expected_missing.why: Companies are expected to periodically test their ability to identify and retrieve product; results would document this practice.
expected_missing.basis: FDA guidance on recall readiness; similar companies maintain mock recall records

expected_missing.title: Third-party audit or food safety assessment report
expected_missing.why: Companies often commission external audits to verify compliance with FSMA or their own customers' food safety requirements.
expected_missing.basis: Industry practice; not a regulatory requirement but common in supply chains

expected_missing.title: Customer complaint or product incident log
expected_missing.why: Documentation of customer reports (e.g., taste, odor, mold, foreign material) provides early warning of process failures and is often linked to product holds or recalls.
expected_missing.basis: Similar food manufacturing companies maintain incident logs

expected_missing.title: Calibration procedures and schedules for monitoring equipment
expected_missing.why: The plan mentions weekly probe thermometer calibration and annual metal detector service, but does not provide detailed procedures (e.g., which calibration solution, which temperature points, who performs it).
expected_missing.basis: FSMA best practice; similar companies have stand-alone calibration SOPs

scan.confidence_notes: High confidence on the document's contents and structure. The document is readable and complete as presented. Moderate confidence on gaps: the FSMA Preventive Controls rule (21 CFR 117) is stable and well-established, and I have checked key thresholds (21 CFR 117.150, 117.155, 117.160) via web search to confirm current requirements. However, I cannot verify from the document alone whether the company has conducted the required annual review of the plan or whether it has met all conditions in practice—only that the plan itself documents certain procedures. I have not seen evidence of the supporting logs or records, which would be held separately. The 16-month age of the plan (effective May 12, 2025; today is September 25, 2026) raises a timing concern: if the plan has not been formally reviewed and re-approved in writing since May 2025, it is likely overdue for the annual review that FSMA and industry practice expect. This is flagged but cannot be confirmed without seeing a dated review memo or revision history.
